questions.q: What is the key difference between a Fabric workspace role and an item permission?
options: A workspace role applies to everything in the workspace; an item permission is confined to a single item
Workspace roles only exist for Admins; item permissions are for everyone else
Item permissions override workspace roles entirely
There is no difference — they are two names for the same thing
questions.explain: Workspace roles (Admin, Member, Contributor, Viewer) apply to every item in that workspace. Item permissions are granted on one item at a time, independent of any workspace role.

questions.q: By default, what permission does sharing a Fabric item always grant the recipient?
options: Read
Edit
Reshare
Execute
questions.explain: Read permission is always included when an item is shared, so the recipient can discover it in the data hub or OneLake catalog and open it.

questions.q: What does the Build permission allow a user to do, and on what kind of item?
options: Create new reports against a semantic model
Compile and deploy a Data Factory pipeline
Construct new tables in a Lakehouse
Assemble a new workspace from a template
questions.explain: Build is specific to semantic models — it lets the recipient create new reports against the model without granting them the ability to edit the model itself.

questions.q: A user has a Viewer role on a workspace AND a direct item-level permission on a report stored in it. If you want to fully revoke their access to that report, what must you do?
options: Remove both the item-level permission and the workspace role — removing just one still leaves them able to view it
Only remove the item-level permission; the workspace role has no effect on items
Only remove the workspace role; item-level permissions expire automatically
Nothing can revoke a Viewer's access once granted
questions.explain: Per Microsoft's own permission-model documentation, a workspace Viewer role alone is enough to see and open a report. Removing only the item permission leaves the workspace role in place, so the user can still view it.

questions.q: What does the "Read all with SQL analytics endpoint" permission on a Lakehouse let a user do?
options: Read lakehouse data through T-SQL via the SQL analytics endpoint without the item's SQL security policy applied
Grant other users Read access automatically
Edit the lakehouse's underlying files directly in OneLake
Create new shortcuts to other lakehouses
questions.explain: This permission lets a recipient query the lakehouse (or warehouse) through the SQL analytics endpoint using T-SQL, without the SQL security policy defined on that endpoint being applied.
